headline: DFW office is stabilizing at elevated vacancy, with rents firming but absorption still thin
thesis: Vacancy remains high at 24.5%, though it is now trending down, and asking rents are rising across the board—$34.04 psf overall and $39.90 psf for Class A. With YTD net absorption only modestly positive at 117K s.f. against 3.3M s.f. of leasing activity, demand is functional but not yet strong enough to materially compress vacancy, while a manageable 2.0M s.f. under construction limits new supply pressure.
what_would_change: A sustained acceleration in net absorption—multiple quarters well above the current 117K YTD pace—pulling vacancy down through the low-20s would turn me constructive; conversely, absorption rolling negative alongside softening rents would push me bearish.
contrarian: The 24.5% headline vacancy invites a bearish read, but the combination of declining vacancy and rising rents—including Class A at $39.90 psf—suggests the market has found a floor rather than continuing to deteriorate.
